title: Master I built an AI music generator with some harnesses
objectives: Generate your first song from a text prompt
Use prompt settings like genre, mood, and tempo to steer output
Run the provided harnesses to batch-generate and evaluate songs

modules.title: Setup and First Song
steps: Install or launch the app, confirm the audio output folder is set, and open the main prompt screen
Type a simple prompt like 'a lo-fi hip hop track with soft piano and rain sounds' and click Generate
Play the result in the built-in preview player and save it to your library

modules.title: Writing Better Prompts
steps: Add genre, mood, instrument, and tempo descriptors to your prompt (e.g., 'upbeat synth-pop, 120 BPM, female vocals')
Generate 3 variations of the same prompt using the variation button and compare which descriptors had the most effect
Save your best-performing prompt as a reusable template in the prompt library

modules.title: Using the Batch Harness
steps: Create a CSV or text file with 5-10 prompts, one per line, following the harness's expected format
Run the batch harness command (or the 'Batch' tab in the UI) and point it at your prompts file
Open the output folder and confirm each prompt produced an audio file and a metadata log

modules.title: Using the Evaluation Harness
steps: Point the evaluation harness at a folder of generated songs from the previous module
Read the harness's report (scores for prompt match, audio quality, or duration) and identify your weakest prompt
Rewrite that one prompt, regenerate the song, and re-run the harness to compare scores

modules.title: Exporting and Sharing
steps: Pick your best song and export it in your preferred format (e.g., MP3 for sharing, WAV for editing)
Rename the exported file using the metadata from the generation log (title, prompt, date)
Set default export settings so future generations save in your chosen format automatically

title: Master Headless Tools
objectives: Navigate the Headless Tools directory and filter by category
Evaluate a listing for agent-readiness (docs, auth, machine-readable specs)
Integrate one directory tool into an AI agent via function calling

modules.title: Find and Shortlist Tools
steps: Open headless.tools and filter the directory by one category you'll actually use (e.g., email, payments, or web scraping)
Open 3 listings and record each tool's base API URL, auth method, and free tier limits in a notes file
Discard any listing whose docs require a human UI flow (OAuth consent screens you can't automate, dashboard-only config)

modules.title: Assess Agent-Readiness
steps: For each shortlisted tool, check its docs for an OpenAPI spec, MCP server, or structured JSON error responses — note which exist
Read the rate limits and webhook docs; write down how an agent would retry a 429 and verify a webhook signature
Pick a winner by scoring the 3 tools 1-5 on spec availability, error format, and idempotency-key support

modules.title: Test the API Headlessly
steps: Sign up for your chosen tool, mint an API key, and store it in a .env file (never hardcode it)
Run the docs' 'hello world' endpoint with curl, piping the response through jq to confirm the JSON shape matches the docs
Deliberately send one malformed request and one request without the key; confirm both return machine-readable error codes

modules.title: Wire It Into an Agent
steps: Write a JSON-schema function definition (name, description, parameters) that wraps the endpoint you tested
Register the function with your agent framework (OpenAI tools, Anthropic tool use, or LangChain) and run a prompt that triggers it
Add a guardrail: cap calls per run, and log the agent's raw tool-call arguments for one test session to catch hallucinated parameters

prerequisites: Comfortable with REST APIs, JSON, and curl or an HTTP client
Understand API key auth and environment variables
Have built at least a basic AI agent or chatbot with tool/function calling
